name: @the-inclusionist/game-platformer
description: The Inclusionist — the platformer. The accessibility-first 2D pixel-art game that the engine was extracted from, now consuming it as a package (ADR-0036, ADR-0068, ADR-0083).
comment:origin: THIS REPOSITORY EXISTS BECAUSE ADR-0036 ORDERED IT ON 2026-08-25, and the code only moved on 06/09.
The record chose `S1 — the game leaves; this repository becomes the engine`, and explicitly REJECTED
`S3 — one monorepo holding engine, shell and every game`. ADR-0058 rejected the monorepo again (T4),
ADR-0068 fixed one repository per game, and ADR-0082 fixed the name `game-<slug>`.
The git history of these files stays in `the-inclusionist-engine`, which is public under AGPL: the move
is a COPY plus a removal, not a history rewrite. Rewriting 200+ commits of interleaved paths to carry
the history across would have risked the engine's own history to gain a `git log` that is one clone away.
comment:dependencies: The engine is a DEPENDENCY, by NAME and by semver — never a `file:` path (ADR-0083 §2, ADR-0036).
⚠️ A `file:` consumer is not a consumer for proof purposes: it reads the engine's folder live, with all
of its devDependencies present, and that is exactly how `6.36.1` shipped unbuildable (ADR-0093).
`pixi.js` is the engine's PEER and is pinned by it to 7.4.2 — two copies would be two renderers arguing
comment:neural-voice: ⚠️ THE NEURAL VOICE IS DECLARED **HERE**, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF ADR-0094. The engine stopped
naming the vendor on 06/09: it arrives through the `carregarVozNeural` port, which `app/js/main.ts`
opens with one line. So the game that WANTS the voice declares the package and pays for it — and the
135.4 MB of `onnxruntime-web` that it drags in as a non-optional peer stop being charged to every
consumer of the engine, including games that will never speak.
⚠️ MEASURED IN THIS VERY MOVE: the first `vite build` here failed with the exact error that made the
engine's `6.36.1` unbuildable — `Rolldown failed to resolve import "@mintplex-labs/piper-tts-web"` —
except pointing at `app/js/main.ts` instead of at the engine's shipped code. That is the port working:
the cost landed on whoever opened it.
🔴 THIS BLOCK SAID «The vendor is DISCONTINUED», AND THAT WAS MEASURED FALSE ON 2026-09-09: no version of
`@mintplex-labs/piper-tts-web` carries a `deprecated` field on npm, and 1.0.5 was published 2026-08-11 —
AFTER ADR-0022 (2026-07-06) declared it dead. The sentence came from that record, attributed to the Dev,
and travelled into six places without any of them measuring it. Its companion claim — «only 2 pt-BR
voices» — is false too: the installed 1.0.4 exposes 118, including all four ADR-0110 names.
⚠️ WHAT IS STILL TRUE IS SHARPER: the bundle pins `HF_BASE` to `huggingface.co/diffusionstudio/piper-voices`
behind a guard that REFUSES any other host, so no school mirror reaches it; and it fetches its own runtime
from cdnjs/jsDelivr by default, which is what ADR-0114 retires. Upstream, Piper moved to
`OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl` and the Open Home Foundation is looking for maintainers.
📌 ADR-0022 still schedules a swap to sherpa-onnx-wasm and issue #129 is where that choice is made — this
note does not make it. When it happens, it is one line in `main.ts` and one line here — not a new version
of the engine for everybody.

scripts.validate: npm run typecheck && vitest run && vite build
